sources.title: Interview note containing usePrevious and UI-update follow-up
Executable history transition model and JavaScript syntax check
Source-first isolated review for render-visible usePrevious

claims.text: The recovered interview source asks first for a usePrevious Hook that records the previous state value and then adds the requirement that changes to that value can trigger UI updates.
React documents that changing ref.current does not trigger a component re-render and that values used for rendering should use state instead.

React documents a conditional setState-during-render pattern for storing information from previous renders, requiring the update to target the currently rendering component and the condition to terminate.
The candidate's two-field history transition preserves previous as the old current when value changes and performs no transition for Object.is-equal input.

boundary_tests.expected: previous is undefined before any earlier value exists

findings: The recovered source contains both the base usePrevious request and the follow-up that changes to the stored previous value must be able to update the UI; the candidate keeps both parts in scope.

React official documentation states that changing ref.current does not trigger a re-render and that information used for rendering should be state, which directly supports moving render-visible history out of a ref-only design.
The candidate avoids the naive setPrevious(value) trap by storing both current and previous, so a state-triggered rerender does not overwrite the meaning of previous with the current input.

React useState documentation explicitly permits the rare conditional set-during-render pattern for storing information from previous renders, provided it updates only the currently rendering component and the condition terminates.
The Object.is guard makes the render-time state adjustment terminating for stable inputs and aligns with React's state equality semantics.

The executable fixture separately validates the pure history transition invariant for initial, changed, unchanged, NaN and signed-zero cases; React-specific render behavior remains grounded in the official docs rather than a fake runtime.
The answer labels initial undefined, return shape, equality rule and object-reference behavior as candidate API choices rather than recovered source facts.
No production project history or hidden React-version claim is fabricated.
